findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the gaskets and interior of the sliding door meat display cooler to be soiled with food debris. The PIC was informed and plans to increase cleaning frequency of the surfaces of the cooler. Ensure the cooler is clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed multiple employees fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. PIC was informed that employees need to use a clean barrier such as a paper towel to turn off the hand sink. This clean barrier prevents cross-contamination during hand washing. Ensure staff are using a barrier when turning off the hand sink.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the triple sink and 3 sanitizer buckets to read 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC stated that the opening shift must have failed to add sanitizer to the mix. The sink and buckets were remade and measured 150ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are testing the sanitizer concentration of the sink and buckets to avoid cross-contamination and food-borne pathogen transmission.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the following items to be out of temperature in the preparation coolers:
1. Sliced tomato (probe 47.4F)
2. Shredded lettuce (probe 53.2F)
3. Sliced tomato (probe 49.9F)

These items in the open-air prep cooler were “mounded” in their containers, which seems to be causing the temperature to be too high. A container of shredded lettuce which was less full measured 37F with the probe from the same cooler. To avoid improper cold holding, avoid “mounding” the food items in their containers when stored in the open-air prep coolers. The shredded lettuce and sliced tomatoes were only in the prep cooler for 1.5 hour. PIC enacted time as a control for those items and will discard after 4 hours. The other container of sliced tomatoes, since the time they were added to the cooler is unknown, was discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed hand sink in back next to mop sink to be blocked by dough rack. Dough rack was moved during inspection. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed interior cavities of drawers of prep cooler to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize interior cavities of prep cooler drawers.

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed wet mop head to be stored head down in mop sink. Store wet mop head in a fashion that promotes quick drying. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed kitchen exhaust hood filters to be soiled with grease and dust. Clean exhaust hood filters.  

6-501.14: (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed knife blade to be stored under scale on kitchen prep line. Knife was placed at 3 compartment sink for wash, rinse and sanitize during inspection. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed shelves above counters on back of prep line to be soiled with sticky residue. Clean and sanitize shelves. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 
Observed the cold holding wells to be holding food between 52F and 60F.  The following items were voluntarily discarded: 50.6 oz of deli turkey, 36.7 oz of pepperoni, 9.2 oz of ham, 18.8 oz of salami and approximately 15 sliced tomatoes. The manager found that the wells had either not been turned on or had been turned off somehow. The facility is working out of the walk in until the glass case comes down to temperature and they can restock it.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM is available at the facility during the inspection. PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is on site at all times food and food contact are being handled.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

A nozzle on the soda fountain drink machine is observed soiled with bacterial build up. PIC is instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation of soilage ont he food contact surfaces of the facility. The nozzle was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The smear knife used for tuna salad is observed laying down in the tuna salad with the handle in direct contact with the food. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the knife removed (to cleaning) during the inspection to correct.
